summary:
[TO BOB NESSj Nov 2  


I am reminded of a song lyric: “scared of living, tired of dying.” Or anyhow that’s how I remember it. Is that any help to you in your travail? Trevail? Travel? Trivia? (No offense meant, but your letters remind me of reading the first sen­ tence of each page of Sunday’s L.A. Times, which runs 436 pages in all. I sort of dig it. “Man crushed by giant U.S. President indicted” and so forth.) My phone number is 714-524'7306, but call late in the day since early in the day (like now) I make little if any sense in what I feel, do and say. If you call me very early I will print out all the dreams I had during the night, and nothing 
duller could be imagined. I say this to warn you, lest you waste your money (it damn well better be your money and not mine; the only people I call in Canada is Jamis, and right now not even her. But I let her call collect. Remember her? Amazing how the flighty ones hang in there when the dependable ones have long since bopped off. I still hear from her. She’s getting her pilot’s license. More power to her.) 

I would very much like to know (in modern, not Biblical sense) your 2nd wife. Yes, we do all remember TENDER IS THE NIGHT, but not with affec­ tion; I remember it with terror, having been married to two psychotic women—-at different times—myself. I could have been Dick Diver reborn: bad karma. 

At 13? Wow. I have mixed feelings about that, some of them Wrong Ones. I know nothing about any meteor. If they ask me I will have...
